context:
The change is entirely in _validate_performance_thresholds. The data collection loop
already captures start_memory and peak_memory and computes the delta - no changes
needed there. Only the assertion and the threshold formula change.

Calibrate threshold conservatively: observed_max_growth * 2 rounded up to nearest
50 MB, with a minimum floor of 100 MB to prevent spurious failures on very fast
machines with aggressive GC.
description:
The TPC-DI scalability test's memory assertion checks absolute process RSS:

  max_memory_mb = 1000 * scale_factor + 2000
  assert metrics["peak_memory_mb"] <= max_memory_mb

This was raised from 600 MB to 2000 MB base in commit 8c0ddcb46 because observed
absolute RSS at SF 0.01 was 1943 MB - xdist workers, loaded modules, and pandas
internals dominate the measurement, not the benchmark itself.

The problem: absolute RSS is immune to memory leaks. A 300 MB regression at SF 0.01
would push actual usage to ~2243 MB, which still passes the 2010 MB ceiling (since
ceiling is 1000*0.01 + 2000 = 2010 MB). The test no longer catches regressions.

The fix is already 90% done: `memory_growth_mb = peak_memory - start_memory` is
already computed and stored in performance_results[scale_factor] at line 144 of
test_multi_scale_factor_performance_analysis. The validation method at line 301
just ignores it, checking peak_memory_mb instead.

Switching to delta restores regression sensitivity: the baseline process RSS
(1800-2000 MB of OS/Python/xdist overhead) is subtracted out, leaving only the
memory actually allocated by the benchmark. A tight ceiling on growth catches leaks
without being affected by CI environment variability.

In _validate_performance_thresholds (line ~301), change:
  max_memory_mb = 1000 * scale_factor + 2000
  assert metrics["peak_memory_mb"] <= max_memory_mb
to:
  max_growth_mb = 1000 * scale_factor + {calibrated_base}
  assert metrics["memory_growth_mb"] <= max_growth_mb
Set {calibrated_base} to observed maximum growth + 2x headroom from w1 results.
Also update the print statement on line 312:
  print(f"  Memory: {metrics['peak_memory_mb']:.1f}MB ✅")
to report growth_mb instead of peak_mb, for clearer test output.
